content.text:
Key facts established:

- **§ 22.1 (p0286):** internal laws of the **State of Wisconsin**, conflicts excluded.
- **§ 22.2 (p0287):** exclusive venue in **Milwaukee County, Wisconsin** state courts and the **E.D. Wis.** — courts, not arbitration.
- **Article 15 (p0227–p0228):** internal executive escalation only; it is not a binding arbitration regime and does not displace litigation.
- **Arbitration references** in p0287 and p0299 are incidental (judgment/award enforcement; fee-shifting) — no arbitration is mandated, and certainly none seated abroad.
- **Direction check (p0293):** Customer, Tri City National Bank, is headquartered at 6400 South 27th Street, **Oak Creek, WI** — inside Milwaukee County. The chosen law and the exclusive venue are our client's own home state and home county, not a forum imposed by the vendor.

Wisconsin is outside the rule's enumerated list (NY/DE/CA/England & Wales), but the material risk the rule guards against — being dragged to the vendor's distant home forum or to foreign arbitration — is absent, and the clause in fact hands us local home-court venue. Redlining to New York would move our own client away from its home forum, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 22.1 Governing Law. The validity, construction and interpretation of this Agreement and the rights and duties of the parties hereto shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of Wisconsin, excluding its principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 selects Wisconsin law and Section 22.2 fixes exclusive venue in the courts of Milwaukee County, Wisconsin and the Eastern District of Wisconsin. Wisconsin is not on the playbook's enumerated list (New York preferred; Delaware, California or England and Wales as fallback), and we note that in passing. It is not a material deviation here: our client, Tri City National Bank, is headquartered in Oak Creek, Wisconsin (Section 22.6 notice block, p0293), inside Milwaukee County, so the governing law and the exclusive forum are our own home jurisdiction and home county rather than a forum imposed by the vendor. The clause therefore falls on the favourable side of the rule's direction and sits well clear of walk-away territory. Disputes go to courts, not arbitration: Article 15 provides only an internal escalation ladder to the parties' CEOs and does not bar or displace litigation, and the arbitration references in Sections 22.2 and 22.11 are incidental (enforcement of a judgment or award, and fee-shifting). There is no arbitration seated abroad and no foreign venue. Redlining to New York would relocate our own client away from its home forum and increase our cost of enforcement, so we do not propose a change.
